Before your first try

  1. Pin Submit Later. Open Chrome's puzzle-piece menu and pin the extension. Click its icon to open the popup.
  2. Use the same Chrome profile. Sign in to the website you want to use, such as Gmail or WhatsApp Web, in that profile. This is separate from a Submit Later account.
  3. Start with a small task. Use a test form or a message to yourself, scheduled a few minutes ahead. Check the result before using an important deadline.

Keep Chrome running and your computer awake. These extension tools work on your computer, with an internet connection. Sleep, shutdown, slow pages or a website signing you out can delay or prevent an action. A schedule is not a guarantee of exact delivery.

One button, one time

Schedule a button you have already prepared

Use this when the email, form or page is ready and only the final click remains.

Example: send a prepared email tomorrow morning

Write the email today, check the recipient and attachments, and schedule the Send button for tomorrow at 9:00 AM.

  1. Open the website and finish filling in the email or form. Keep the final button visible.
  2. Click the Submit Later icon, then Pick a button to schedule. You can also use the shortcut shown in the popup.
  3. Move your pointer over the button. Check the highlighted area, then select it. The picker opens a scheduling dialog.
  4. Choose Press it in this tab. Select a quick time such as Tomorrow 9 AM, or enter a future date and time. Check the displayed date carefully; times use your computer's timezone.
  5. Click Schedule. Open the extension popup and check that the correct page, button and time appear in the upcoming list.
  6. Keep that tab open and unchanged until it runs. Do not refresh it, navigate away, discard the draft or sign out. Afterwards, check the website's confirmation or Sent folder.

Need to change something? Cancel the upcoming schedule first, update the page, then pick the button and schedule it again. Dates must be in the future and within 30 days.

A fresh page at the chosen time

Reopen a page and press a button

Example: open a weekly meeting page

Schedule its Join button for Monday at 9:55 AM. Check whether the meeting site also asks you to choose a microphone or confirm joining.

  1. Visit the page and use Pick a button to schedule to select its button.
  2. Choose Reopen this page and press it. Allow access to this site when Chrome asks.
  3. Set the first date and time. Under Repeat, choose Never, Every day, Every weekday (Mon–Fri) or Every week.
  4. Click Schedule and check the upcoming entry. You can close the original website tab; keep Chrome running, the computer awake and your website account signed in.

The page opens fresh. This mode does not refill an email or form you typed earlier. For tasks that need typing, several clicks or a dropdown selection, use Action Flows.

Automate actions on a web page

Record a task, then review the steps

An Action Flow is an ordered list of actions. For example: open your reporting page, choose a department, enter a date and download a report.

  1. Open the extension popup and choose Automate actions on a web page. On the Action Flows page, click + New flow.
  2. Give it a useful name, such as “Prepare weekly sales report”. Enter the starting website address, including https://.
  3. Click Allow on this site and accept Chrome's permission request for that site.
  4. Choose Record it (easiest). In the tab that opens, do the task slowly: click a control, enter its value, then wait for the page to respond before continuing.
  5. For an autocomplete field, type the search first, wait for suggestions, then select the exact result. Simply clicking a suggestion that was already on screen may leave out the search needed to recreate it.
  6. Use Undo last in the recording bar to remove a mistaken recorded step. This removes the step from the flow; it does not undo what happened on the website.
  7. Click Done in the recording bar. Review the editor from top to bottom. Check every field, value, selected item and page address.
  8. Choose Only when I press Run for your first try. Click Save, then Test run. Use Open the tab to inspect the actual page and check the step results.

Recording performs your clicks on the real website. Stop before sending, paying or submitting during a practice recording. Test run also performs ordinary actions; it holds actions it recognizes as final. It cannot recognize every website's behavior. Use a test account or a harmless task, and add an Ask me step before anything you want to review yourself.

Recording and editing use no guest allowance. Each run, including Test run, uses one guest schedule. Read the Action Flows walkthrough ↑

Worked example · a draft you can inspect

Prepare a Gmail follow-up

Start with a draft, without sending it. Use your own email address for the recipient so you can check the whole sequence.

  1. Sign in to Gmail in this Chrome profile. Close extra compose windows so there is only one recipient field to find.
  2. Create a new flow called “Prepare follow-up draft”. Use your Gmail inbox address as the starting page, allow the site and choose Record it (easiest).
  3. In the recording tab, click Gmail's Compose. Click the To field and type your own email address.
  4. Wait for Gmail's matching suggestion, then select it. Confirm that Gmail shows the address as a recipient chip.
  5. Enter the subject “Tomorrow's meeting” and the message “Hi, here are the notes for our meeting tomorrow.” Click Done on the recording bar before pressing Send.
  6. In the editor, check that the order is Open → Click Compose → Type recipient → Select recipient → Type subject → Type message. The recipient Type step must be present.
  7. Save, then close the draft's compose window before testing, so the replay starts from the inbox again. Click Test run and inspect the newly prepared draft.

What you should see: one compose window with the intended recipient chip, subject and message. This example leaves the draft unsent.

Ready to include sending? Add an Ask me step to review the draft, followed by a Click step picked on Gmail's Send button. Save, then click Run now with your own address as the recipient. Read each confirmation before continuing, then check Gmail's Sent folder.

If “To recipients” or a suggestion cannot be found, follow the Gmail troubleshooting steps. Re-record old steps that never captured the recipient query.

Make the task your own

Build or edit a flow step by step

  1. For a new flow, enter its name and website, allow access, then choose Build it step by step. To change a saved flow, open its editor from the Flows list.
  2. Click + Add a step and choose the action you need. Open the step to see its details.
  3. For a field or button, click Pick on the page and select the real control. If it only appears after another action, first open that part of the page yourself.
  4. For Type, enter the text. For Choose, enter the dropdown option. For Wait until it appears, pick the expected item and set the maximum wait.
  5. Use ↑ Up or ↓ Down to change the order, Pick again to replace a target, and Delete step to remove an action. Record more on the site adds another recorded sequence.
  6. Leave If it can't be done → Stop and tell me selected for essential steps. If entering a recipient fails, the flow should stop before reaching Send.
  7. Click Save, test from the normal starting page, and check both the step log and the actual website.
Which action should I choose?
Open a page
Navigate to a page on the flow's allowed website.
Click / Type / Choose / Tick
Press a control, fill a text field, select a native dropdown option, or set a checkbox. Custom dropdowns often need a Click to open them and another Click to choose an item.
Wait until it appears / Wait
Wait for a specific item to be available, or pause for a fixed number of seconds. Prefer waiting for the item on pages that load at different speeds.
Scroll to / Press a key
Bring an item into view, or use Enter, Tab or Escape. Enter may submit a form or send a message; check what it does on your site.
Ask me
Pause for your approval or for you to do something yourself, such as entering a one-time code.
Tell me / Done / Stop
Show a notification and continue; finish with a successful result; or end because there is nothing to do.

From a successful test to a routine

Choose when a flow runs

  1. Open the flow editor and find When to run. Use Only when I press Run for manual use, or Once for a single future date.
  2. For a routine, choose Every day, Weekdays or Weekly, then enter its time and any requested day. Check the next-run preview.
  3. For periodic checks during part of a day, choose Repeat between times. Set the time window and interval; repeats must be at least 10 minutes apart.
  4. Use Stop after N runs when the routine should end after a set number of runs. For example, run a weekday report five times, then stop.
  5. In Safety & alerts, choose whether success should ring, notify you or stay quiet. Click Save and turn on to enable the schedule.
  6. Return to the Flows list to check its next run. Use its On or off switch to disable or enable scheduled runs. During an active run, use Stop; pausing a schedule is not the same as stopping the current run.
Example: download a Friday report

Record opening your reporting page, selecting the report and clicking Download. Test the selection and inspect the downloaded file. Choose Weekly, Friday, 4:00 PM, then turn it on. The last click of a repeating flow asks for confirmation, so be available to approve it.

One flow runs at a time. Space schedules apart. A flow pauses after repeated failures or a site's request to slow down; open its result and fix the cause before resuming. A run can last up to 15 minutes, including waits. Chrome must stay open and the computer awake.

Optional · after your first flow works

Add a condition, a loop or changing values

Only do something when the page is ready
  1. Add Only if…. Choose a condition such as this appears, this can be clicked or the page says….
  2. Pick the item or enter the words to check. For example, check whether your report page says “Report ready”.
  3. Add Tell me inside the condition, with “Your report is ready”. Enable Otherwise if you want different steps when it is not ready.
  4. Test both cases: once with the condition true and once without it. Check that only the intended branch runs.
Repeat steps for items in a list
  1. Add Repeat for each…. Choose a list/calendar or dropdown, then pick the items on the page.
  2. Set Try at most (items) to a small number for the first test. Choose whether to stop at the first item that works or process all of them.
  3. Add the actions inside the loop. Use {item} in a target's Its words field when it should match the current item.
  4. Test with two harmless items and inspect their order before using the whole list.
Check again until something changes

Keep trying until… repeats its enclosed actions until a condition is met. Pick the condition, set Try at most (times) and choose at least 60 seconds between tries. Put the action that refreshes the information inside the loop; waiting alone does not refresh a static page.

For example, reopen a report-status page and check for “Report ready”. Use a small retry limit within the 15-minute run limit. For checks over several hours, use Repeat between times instead.

Use a different value on each run
  1. Open a Type or Choose step and select Use a different value on each run (or option for Choose).
  2. Use + Add a value to enter one value per row, in order. Example: three report categories, one for each scheduled run.
  3. Check the next value shown in the editor. Under When the per-run values run out, choose turn the flow off to stop at the end, or start again from the first to reuse the list.
  4. Review the run count and value preview after testing, before enabling your real schedule.

Use Ask me for passwords, verification codes and payment details. Recognized private fields are not recorded as saved values. Review your recorded text before saving; ordinary field values stay on this computer.

A reminder from your WhatsApp account

Schedule a message, photo or video

Example: tomorrow's meeting reminder

Send yourself “Reminder: team meeting at 10. Please bring the project notes.” tomorrow at 9:00 AM. Once that works, use it for people who expect to hear from you.

  1. Sign in to WhatsApp Web in the same Chrome profile. Open the extension's WhatsApp scheduler and select Compose.
  2. Under Who should get it?, search a saved contact or enter a full phone number including its country code, then click Add. Check the recipient chip; remove any unintended person.
  3. Under What should it say?, write your message. To attach media, click Add photo or video and choose a file up to 16 MB. The text becomes its caption.
  4. Use + Add another message for a sequence of up to five messages to each person. To send the same sequence to several people, add them to the recipient list, up to 20 people.
  5. Set Send at and Repeat. For your first try, choose a few minutes ahead and Never. Read the schedule summary, then click Schedule message and allow WhatsApp Web access if asked.
  6. Check Scheduled messages below. Keep Chrome running, the computer awake and WhatsApp Web signed in. At the time, the extension opens or reloads WhatsApp Web.
  7. Check the actual chat afterwards. A click or an extension result does not prove that WhatsApp delivered or read the message.

Recipients are processed one by one, usually 20–45 seconds apart. A group of recipients will not all receive the message at the exact start time. The extension limits sending to 100 messages a day; follow WhatsApp's rules and message people who expect it.

Send a different message or time to each person

Choose Batch. In each row, select a contact or full phone number, enter that person's message and set Send at. Click + Add row for another person. Same time for all rows copies the time; simultaneous rows are still spaced out. Review every row, then click Schedule all.

Example: one colleague gets “Please review the slides” at 9:00, and another gets “Please check the demo” at 9:15. Use Compose when everyone should get the same messages or attachments.

To change a scheduled message: cancel it in Scheduled messages, then create the corrected schedule. Check existing entries before retrying after a slow response, so you do not schedule duplicates.

Read the WhatsApp walkthrough ↑

Find people without retyping numbers

Import and manage contacts

  1. Open the WhatsApp scheduler and scroll to Your contacts. Export contacts from your address book as a .vcf or .csv file, or make a CSV with Name and Phone columns.
  2. Use full international numbers where possible. If your file contains local numbers without a country code, select the correct country under Who should get it? before importing.
  3. Click Import contacts, select the file and read the import result. Check a few names and complete numbers before scheduling anything.
  4. Search by name or number. Use a contact's edit or delete control to correct it, or Add contact to create one manually.
  5. Return to Compose, search for a name and select the result. Verify its recipient chip before scheduling.

Contacts are stored in this extension on this computer; they are not uploaded to Submit Later. Deleting a contact does not cancel a message you already scheduled for that number. Cancel the message separately if needed.

Know what happened

Check, cancel or reschedule a task

Button presses and reopened pages
Open the extension popup to see upcoming tasks and recent results. Use the upcoming task's cancel control before it runs. To change its time, cancel and create a new schedule.
WhatsApp messages
Use Scheduled messages on the WhatsApp page. Cancel removes an upcoming recipient's schedule; Cancel all removes an upcoming group. A message already being sent cannot be recalled here.
Action Flows
Open Runs for step-by-step results. Open the saved flow to edit it. Stop an active run before changing its steps, then save and test the updated flow.
Failed or uncertain results
Read the message and inspect the website before retrying. A send might have happened even if the extension could not confirm it. Check Sent or the chat first to avoid duplicates.

Stopping is not undoing. Stop prevents later flow actions; it cannot reverse a click, message or submission that has already happened. After a browser interruption, inspect the last result and the website rather than assuming the task will replay.

Try first, connect when you need more

Guest access and your account

You can try nine schedules without signing in to Submit Later, shared across button presses, reopen-and-press, WhatsApp, repeats and Action Flows. Each WhatsApp recipient, repeat occurrence or flow run (including a test) uses one schedule. Recording and editing a flow are free.

  1. Check your remaining guest uses in the extension. Start with one recipient or one flow run so you can see how it works.
  2. When you need more, use the extension's account link to create an account or log in. Finish in the same Chrome profile so the website connects to this installation.
  3. Return to the popup or extension connection in your account and check the signed-in email and plan. New accounts receive the current trial shown there.

Advanced extension features are included during the trial and with Button Scheduler Pro. Check your account for current allowances, expiry and pricing. Signing in does not copy your saved flows, contacts or tasks to another computer.

Looking for Timed Forms or Webhook Scheduler? Those are separate tools in your Submit Later website account. Open your account from the extension, then choose the tool in the dashboard. Follow the Timed Forms and Webhook Scheduler walkthroughs below for the web tools.

Set up your workspace

Settings that help

In the extension popup, open Settings to adjust the options below.

Reliable clicking
Uses a real mouse-style click for sites that ignore a simple click. Chrome may show a debugging banner while it works.
Bring tab forward
Helps you see the page when a button task runs. Avoid interacting with a tab while an automated task is using it.
Keep computer awake
Requests that the computer stay awake while work is pending. It cannot run Chrome after shutdown or guarantee that a closed laptop stays awake.
Reminders, shortcut and theme
Choose your reminder preference and default time offset, check or change the picker shortcut, and select a colour theme or light/dark appearance.

Web tool · no extension needed

Import a Google Form and set its response window

Example: workshop registration

Open registration on Monday at 9:00 AM, close it on Friday at 5:00 PM, and show the form inside your organization's website.

  1. Open Timed Forms in your account. Connect the Google account that can edit your form and approve the requested access. You do not need your own developer keys.
  2. Click + New timed form. Paste the Google Form URL, import it and review the preview. Use a form you own or have permission to edit.
  3. Enter a Display name. Under Response window, choose Opens on, the closing date and the correct Timezone. Check the complete dates, not just the times.
  4. Under Hosted page design, set the organization name, introduction, accent, background, wrapper card and text colours. Review the preview. These settings style the surrounding page; Google controls the embedded form fields.
  5. Save the form, then open its detail page. Under Questions, use + Add question or an existing question's edit/remove controls for supported question types. These changes also affect the connected Google Form.
  6. Use Preview to inspect the hosted page. Check its window and Google response-control status before sharing the link. Use Sync Google if you need to retry synchronization.
Embed the timed form on your website
  1. Open Edit design & timing and enable Enable website embedding.
  2. Enter your Approved website origins, for example https://www.example.org. An origin is the scheme and domain, without a page path. Include each actual site origin you will use.
  3. Choose an embed height and save. In Embed on your website, click Copy embed code.
  4. Paste the code into your website editor's HTML/embed block. Preview the published page and check that the countdown, live form and closed page fit.

Test the deadline at Google too. An embed does not hide the underlying Google Form URL. Managed imports enforce the window by synchronizing Google's accepting-responses setting. Check both the hosted page and the original form after closing. Legacy links alone do not close the Google Form.

If Google connection is unavailable, contact support with the message shown. If Google asks you to sign in again, reconnect from Timed Forms. Your browser can be closed once a managed form is saved; the server handles the response-window changes.

Web tool · runs on the server

Schedule an HTTPS request

Example: start a weekday report

Have your own reporting service generate a summary at 8:30 AM on weekdays. First use a test endpoint you control so you can inspect the request.

  1. Open Webhook Scheduler in your account and click New job.
  2. In Request, name the job and enter the full HTTPS endpoint. Select the method your service expects, such as GET or POST. Add its required headers and request body.
  3. In Schedule, choose a one-time or recurring schedule and its timezone. Review the next-run date and time. Use weekdays for the report example.
  4. Review and save the job. Open its details and check the request and schedule before letting it run.
  5. To check the integration immediately, use Run now with your test endpoint. This sends a real request. Inspect the execution log's status, duration and response preview.
  6. Check the receiving service for the expected report or event. Use Pause to stop future scheduled runs while changing or troubleshooting the job, then resume when ready.

If a run fails: read the recorded error, check the endpoint and credentials, and verify whether the receiving service performed any action before retrying. A successful HTTP response is evidence that the endpoint replied; it does not prove every downstream task finished.

Webhook schedules run on the server, so you can close Chrome. Keep credentials out of screenshots and public links, and use an endpoint that you are authorized to call.

Get back on track

Something did not work as expected

Gmail's To field or recipient suggestion cannot be found
  1. Stop the run. Check that Gmail is signed in and the compose window is open in the flow's tab.
  2. Close other compose windows. Confirm the flow includes Type with the full recipient query before selecting the suggestion.
  3. Open the failing step and use Pick again on the visible recipient input or exact suggestion. If the query was never recorded, re-record that part: type, wait for suggestions, select the matching address, then click Done.
  4. If Compose loads slowly, add Wait until it appears after Click Compose and pick a visible compose control such as Subject. Then try the recipient step again.
  5. Test with your own address and check the recipient chip before approving any Send action.
A button or field cannot be found

Open the flow's tab and check the page it actually reached. Is there a login screen, a cookie notice, a closed menu or a changed layout? Open the needed part of the page and use Pick again on the failing step. Add Wait until it appears when the page needs time to load. Keep essential steps on Stop and tell me.

The flow is waiting or asks for confirmation

Choose Open the tab. Read the Continue/Stop bar, complete the requested task and press Continue only when ready. An Ask me step or recognized final action can wait for your approval; CAPTCHAs must be completed by you. The confirmation wait is limited to 10 minutes and the whole run to 15 minutes. If there is sound but no notification, check Chrome's notification permission in your computer settings; the on-page bar still works.

The scheduled time passed but nothing happened

Check the result first. Was Chrome running, the computer awake, the website signed in and the internet connected? For Press it in this tab, the original tab must remain open and unchanged. Check your computer's timezone and the saved date. Restore site permission if requested, inspect the website for a partial result, then create a small test schedule.

WhatsApp did not send, or only some people received it

Check each recipient's result and the actual chats. Sign in to WhatsApp Web if needed, verify country codes and check attached file sizes. An existing unsent draft can stop the task to avoid overwriting it; finish or clear that draft yourself. Retry only recipients you have confirmed were not sent a message.

I signed in, but the extension still asks me to log in

Open Account from the extension you are using and log in again in that Chrome profile. Check that you have not opened the website in another browser/profile or enabled two copies of Submit Later. Return to the extension's Account page and check its email and plan. If it still fails, use Contact support.

The picker does not open on this page

Try a normal website tab. Chrome's internal pages and the Chrome Web Store restrict extension access. For an embedded page, the extension may need permission for its site too. If a website changes address during recording, return to Action Flows and review the site-access prompt.

Still stuck? Open Contact support. Include the feature, the step that failed, the exact error and what you could see on the page. Keep passwords, verification codes and private message contents out of your report.
